answer: Each agent identity earns standing only through verified work that peers sign, like a lantern hung on a public record, so a fake identity starts with nothing. To open a vault of shared resources, an agent must first complete small, costly tasks whose deposits vest slowly, tying each new identity to real effort. A sybil swarm would need to fund and sustain many such slow identities at once — chasing a comet across the sky — while one honest agent builds the same trust with a single identity and steady output.
